t: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon was the first political philosopher to call himself an anarchist and give the word a positive meaning; in early English usage it had stood for disorder.

Expelled from the First International by the Marxists at the Hague Congress of 1872, the anarchists formed their own St. Imier International; Bakunin predicted that revolutionaries who took power on Marx’s terms would become the workers’ new tyrants.

In the Spanish Revolution of 1936 an anarchist-inspired movement took control of Barcelona and collectivised the land across rural Spain; the end of the Spanish Civil War closed the classical era of anarchism.
dyk: In 1901 the Catalan anarchist Francisco Ferrer founded the Escuela Moderna in Barcelona, a secular school free of both state and church; it closed after constant harassment by the state, but inspired modern schools around the world.
ev: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon publishes What Is Property?, describing his goal as a synthesis of communism and property
Anarchists take part in the Paris Commune, which becomes an inspiration for the anarcho-communists
The Bakuninists are expelled from the First International at the Hague Congress and found the St. Imier International
Fernando Tarrida del Mármol calls for an anarchism without adjectives, uniting the rival schools
The United States passes the Immigration Act of 1903, also called the Anarchist Exclusion Act
Anarchists take part in the Russian Revolution against the White movement, above all in the Makhnovshchina
In the Spanish Revolution anarchists and syndicalists of the CNT and FAI take control of Barcelona and collectivise land
Anarchists, leading networks of the anti-globalisation movement, take part in the confrontations at the Seattle WTO conference

f.thinkers: William Godwin, of philosophical anarchism; Max Stirner, of individualism; Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, first to call himself an anarchist and theorist of mutualism; Mikhail Bakunin, founder of collectivist anarchism; Peter Kropotkin, Russian philosopher and scientist and theorist of anarcho-communism; Errico Malatesta and Emma Goldman; Leo Tolstoy, Christian anarchist
f.texts: William Godwin’s Political Justice; Pierre-Joseph Proudhon’s What Is Property? (1840); Max Stirner’s “The False Principle of Our Education”; Leo Tolstoy’s essay Education and Culture
f.ideas: abolition of the state; opposition to capitalism and every form of coercive authority; free association and voluntary federation; mutual aid and reciprocity; workers’ self-management; direct action and the unity of means and ends
f.today: resurgent since the late 20th century within anti-capitalist, anti-war and anti-globalisation movements; affinity groups, black blocs, Food Not Bombs and self-managed social centres; an influence on the Zapatistas in Mexico and on Rojava, the Democratic Federation of Northern Syria
